#Title :  Analysisis of line list and coverage DATASETS: 'Coverage_data_EN’ and ‘Case_data_EN

# Date ; 18/09/2026

# Made by: Evrard Melvin Kepgang Nanseu

# Output : analysis of the epidemiological situation (Person, Tine , Place ) in relation with coverage

#Purpose :  This script is the script used to analyse the datasets ‘Coverage_data_EN’ and ‘Case_data_EN'
#           This is done in view of presenting the SITREP of outbreak and vaccine coverege in Province X.


# This script will be an automated script which at a moment will need the import(selection) of the data set,
# as the data may increase over time. The packages needed for this script to run will be added as well and #the output can be obtained directly and the graphs will be saves automatically.

```{r}
#Loading packages
install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(openxlsx2, lubridate, readxl, ggplot2, tidyverse, scales)
library(dplyr)
#importing the data set
case <- read_excel("Kepgang Nanseu, Evrard Melvin - Workbook.xlsx", sheet = "DATA_CASE")
coverage <- read_excel("Kepgang Nanseu, Evrard Melvin - Workbook.xlsx", sheet = "DATA_COVERAGE")

```

```{r}

# Descriptive statistics counts and proportions
case %>% dplyr::count(year) # Cases from 2021 -2026
outbreak <- case %>% filter(year=="2026")   # number of cases in 2026
outbreak %>% count(sex)%>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))
outbreak %>% count(age_group)%>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))
outbreak %>% count(region)%>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))
outbreak %>% count(exposure_setting)%>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))
outbreak %>% count(acquisition)

case %>% count(sex)
case %>% count(age_group)
case %>% count(region)

outbreak %>%
  count(age_group, sex)

case %>% filter(year!="2026") %>% count(acquisition)

 
```


```{r}
# confirming the outbreak
# 1. Cases per year
cases_year <- case %>% count(year, name = "cases")
cases_year

# 2. Baseline: average number of cases per year in 2021-2025
baseline_mean <- cases_year %>%
  filter(year != "2026") %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(cases)) %>%
  pull(mean)

# 3. How many times higher is 2026?
cases_2026 <- cases_year %>% filter(year == "2026") %>% pull(cases)
ratio <- round(cases_2026 / baseline_mean, 1)
ratio
```

#Epi curve
```{r}
# Highlighting the informations in 2026

plot <- ggplot(outbreak, aes(x = as.Date(report_date), fill = acquisition)) +
  geom_bar(width = 1) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = sort(unique(as.Date(outbreak$report_date))), date_labels = "%d %b") +
  labs(x = "Date of report", y = "Number of cases", title = "Number of cases by date of report and source of infection",
     subtitle = "Province X, 1 January - 30 June 2026 (n = 63)", size = 6) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 11), 
        plot.title    = element_text(size = 22, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.text   = element_text(size = 14))
plot

ggsave("epicurve_2026.png", plot, width = 24, height = 8, dpi = 150, bg = "white")

#Highlighting the situation since 2021
case <- case %>%
     mutate(week = floor_date(report_date, "week", week_start = 7))
plot1 <- ggplot(case, aes(x = week, fill = acquisition)) +
  geom_bar() +  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y")+
  labs(x = "Period", y = "Number of cases", title = "Number of cases by date of report and source of infection",
     subtitle = "Province X, 2021 - 30 June 2026 (n = 77)") +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 11), 
        plot.title    = element_text(size = 22, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16))
plot1
ggsave("epicurve_2021_2026.png", plot1, width = 26, height = 8, dpi = 150, bg = "white")


```


# Checking the link with vaccination coverage at the group level

```{r}
# Grouping data per region to allow merging and computation per region
cases_region <- outbreak %>% count(region, name = "cases")

pop_region <- coverage %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(population = sum(population_2025),
            vaccinated = sum(n_vaccinated))

region_table <- pop_region %>%
  left_join(cases_region, by = "region") %>%
  mutate(cases = replace_na(cases, 0))

#  Province (one row)
Province <- region_table %>%
  summarise(region = "Province", cases = sum(cases),
            population = sum(population), vaccinated = sum(vaccinated))

# Regions + Province in one table, then the measures
region_calc <- region_table %>%
  bind_rows(Province) %>%
  mutate(attack_rate  = round(cases / population * 100000, 1),
         coverage     = round(vaccinated / population * 100, 1),
         unvaccinated = population - vaccinated,
         pct_cases    = round(cases / Province$cases * 100, 1),
         region       = factor(region, levels = region))      

region_calc

# Plot: regions in blue, province in red
plot2 <- ggplot(region_calc, aes(x = region, y = attack_rate, fill = region == "Province")) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(attack_rate, " (cov. ", coverage, "%)")),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "steelblue", "TRUE" = "red"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Attack rate (per 100,000) and vaccine coverage by region, Province X, 1 January – 30 June 2026", 
       x = "Region", y = "Attack rate per 100,000") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

plot2

ggsave("Attack rate_region.png", plot2, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 150, bg = "white")



```




# Checking the link with vaccination covergae per age group

```{r}
 cases_age <- outbreak %>% count(age_group, name = "cases")

pop_age <- coverage %>%
  group_by(age_group) %>%
  summarise(population = sum(population_2025),
            vaccinated = sum(n_vaccinated))

age_table <- pop_age %>%
  left_join(cases_age, by = "age_group") %>%
  mutate(cases = replace_na(cases, 0))

# Province (one row)
Province_age <- age_table %>%
  summarise(age_group = "Province", cases = sum(cases),
            population = sum(population), vaccinated = sum(vaccinated))

# Age groups + Province in one table, then the measures
age_calc <- age_table %>%
  bind_rows(Province_age) %>%
  mutate(attack_rate  = round(cases / population * 100000, 1),
         coverage     = round(vaccinated / population * 100, 1),
         unvaccinated = population - vaccinated,
         pct_cases    = round(cases / Province_age$cases * 100, 1),
         age_group    = factor(age_group, levels = age_group))      

age_calc

# Plot: age groups in blue, Province in red
plot3 <- ggplot(age_calc, aes(x = age_group, y = attack_rate, fill = age_group == "Province")) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(attack_rate, "\n(cov. ", coverage, "%)")),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 5.5, lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "steelblue", "TRUE" = "red"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Attack rate (per 100,000) and vaccine coverage by age group, Province X, 1 January – 30 June 2026",
       x = "Age group (years)", y = "Attack rate per 100,000") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

plot3

ggsave("attack_rate_age.png", plot3, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
```
# Does vaccination in different regions vary per age group and affects attack rate?
```{r}
cases_region_age <- outbreak %>% count(region,age_group, name = "cases")

pop_region_age <- coverage %>% group_by(region, age_group) %>%  summarise(population = sum(population_2025),
                                         vaccinated = sum(n_vaccinated))
pop_reg_age_table <- pop_region_age %>%  left_join(cases_region_age, by = c("region","age_group"))

pop_reg_age_table <- pop_reg_age_table %>%
  mutate(attack_rate  = round(cases / population * 100000, 1),
         coverage     = round(vaccinated / population * 100, 1),
         unvaccinated = population - vaccinated,
         pct_cases    = round(cases / sum(cases) * 100, 1))
```

# Plotting this result
```{r}
plot4 <- ggplot(pop_reg_age_table, aes(x = age_group, y = region, fill = coverage)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(coverage, "%\n", cases, " cases"))) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "red", high = "lightyellow") +
  labs(title = "Vaccine coverage and number of cases by region and age group",
     subtitle = "Province X: coverage at end of 2025; cases reported 1 January – 30 June 2026",
       x = "Age group", y = "Region", fill = "Coverage (%)") +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 11),
        axis.text.y = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, size = 11),
        plot.title    = element_text(size = 22, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.text   = element_text(size = 14))
plot4
ggsave("region group.png", plot4, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
```


# Checking if source of exposure explains the outbreak
```{r}
# Describing the clusters (exposure settings)
clusters <- outbreak %>%
  filter(!is.na(exposure_setting)) %>%
  group_by(exposure_setting) %>%
  summarise(cases        = n(),
            first_report = min(as.Date(report_date)),
            last_report  = max(as.Date(report_date)),
            min_age      = min(age),
            max_age      = max(age),
            median_age   = median(age),
            regions      = paste(sort(unique(region)), collapse = ", "))

clusters

# How many cases in each region, per cluster?
outbreak %>%
  filter(!is.na(exposure_setting)) %>%
  count(exposure_setting, region)

# Locally acquired cases with no setting recorded
outbreak %>%
  filter(acquisition == "locally acquired", is.na(exposure_setting)) %>%
  nrow()
```
